definition: The circle of radius $1$ centred at the origin, $x^{2} + y^{2} = 1$; the point on it at angle $\theta$ from the positive $x$-axis is $(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$.
One of the four regions the $x$- and $y$-axes split the plane into, numbered first to fourth anticlockwise from the top right.
The acute angle between the $x$-axis and the line from the origin to the point on the unit circle; it fixes the size of a trig value, while the quadrant fixes its sign.
When two sides of a triangle and an angle not between them are known, the sine rule can give an acute and an obtuse angle, so two different triangles may fit.
